ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT rules are contained in the French Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 to R.561-63, implementing EU AML requirements. Beneficial-owner identification and filing for legal entities are governed principally by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and R.561-55 to R.561-63 of that Code, together with Articles 40 and 41 of Decree No. 2021-1097 of 19 August 2021 and relevant provisions of the French Commercial Code. The beneficial-owner register is maintained through the Registre National des Entreprises and the Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle. French rules also derive from Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843, subject to subsequent EU and French amendments.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, onboarding, banking, and material transactions, identify and document all direct and indirect owners, controllers, directors, authorized signatories, agents, and key counterparties. Screen against United Nations Security Council lists, EU financial sanctions, French national measures, OFAC lists where the transaction, currency, person, bank, or nexus creates U.S. exposure, and relevant domestic PEP and adverse-media sources. Apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs and their family members or known close associates under Articles L.561-10 and L.561-10-1 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Establish source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, senior-management approval, transaction monitoring, five-year record retention under Article L.561-12, and suspicious-transaction reporting to TRACFIN under Article L.561-15. Screening must cover transliteration variants, aliases, beneficial owners below the filing threshold where control exists, and sanctioned vessels, freight intermediaries, and logistics counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the company is registered in the Registre National des Entreprises and, for commercial activities, in the relevant Registre du commerce et des sociétés.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the incorporation documents and filing in accordance with French company-law requirements. French characters and Latin-script names are accepted; a foreign-language name may be used if it is not misleading, unlawful, contrary to public policy, or confusingly similar to an existing protected name. The legal form or an accepted abbreviation, including SAS, must be shown in the corporate documentation and relevant commercial disclosures. Name availability does not itself create trademark rights. Search the RNE, RCS, INPI trademark database, EUIPO database, domain-name registers, and relevant business directories before filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: European Union references or official institutional designations
Any term implying a regulated activity, public authority, monopoly, or official affiliation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory company-name reservation procedure or universal 30-day statutory reservation period. A 30-day period is an operational hold only where a professional intermediary or filing workflow offers one and does not guarantee registration. File the SAS incorporation through the INPI Guichet unique with the proposed name, legal-form designation, business description, registered-office evidence, and supporting corporate documents. If the filing is rejected or suspended, obtain the electronic rejection notice, identify the legal or documentary defect, and submit corrected documents through the prescribed INPI workflow within the stated deadline. For a formal administrative decision by a competent authority, request reconsideration from the issuing authority or file a hierarchical appeal; judicial review may be brought before the competent administrative or judicial court depending on the decision. A registered trademark infringement, unfair competition, or confusing corporate-name dispute requires separate action before the competent civil or commercial court. A rejected name may be replaced by a new proposed name after a fresh availability and trademark search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office under Articles L.123-11 and following of the French Commercial Code. Commercial domiciliation is permitted through an authorized domiciliation company subject to Articles L.123-11-2 to L.123-11-5 and related regulatory requirements. A virtual office is generally acceptable for registration and corporate correspondence but is weak evidence of commercial substance for a cross-border express courier business. The company should maintain accessible operational records, management availability, customer and carrier contracts, customs and transport documentation, accounting records, and evidence of actual French activity. If the company operates vehicles or performs regulated road transport, a virtual office alone will not satisfy operational, licensing, vehicle, storage, or transport-manager requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated risk: 10% to 20% during the first 12 months for an ordinary low-risk registration, increasing to approximately 25% to 40% where the filing uses a domiciliation address, involves non-resident shareholders, has complex ownership, presents customs or sanctions exposure, or applies for transport-related authorization. These are risk estimates, not statutory probabilities. Relevant authorities may conduct verification or request evidence of premises and activity, including the INPI/RNE administration, tax administration, customs, labor authorities, URSSAF, ARCEP, and transport authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and the official tax portal at impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing a French SAS must register with the INSEE to obtain a SIREN number, followed by VAT registration with the DGFiP. The process includes filing incorporation documents, obtaining SIRET code, and submitting tax registration forms via the guichet-entreprises or online portal. Statutory TIN is the SIREN combined with VAT number FR followed by 9 digits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not offer check-the-box elections. SAS entities are subject to entity-level taxation under the French corporate tax regime. Hybrid mismatch rules are governed by EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and domestic provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for all B2B transactions in France through the national e-invoicing platform. Real-time fiscal clearance via API integration with the PEPITES system. Digital time-stamping and QR code stamping required for compliant invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for 0% VAT rate on exports of goods or services provided to non-EU customers. Requires proof that the transaction is an export outside the European Union, including commercial invoice indicating export destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU or EDIS), Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document, Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of fraudulent export zero-rating are subject to penalties of up to 80% of the evaded VAT, interest charges, and potential criminal liability. Retrospective clawback applies with surtaxes for non-compliant claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the European System of Central Banks and the Eurosystem; prudential supervision is delegated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), while exchange-policy interpretation and regulatory implementation rest with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility is guaranteed for both current and capital account transactions under Article 63 TFEU (free movement of capital) and French law. Inbound capital injection into an SAS and outward profit remittance require no prior exchange-control authorization or visa. Funds must transit through an ACPR-supervised institution or a passported EEA payment institution. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders may be subject to the 30% flat tax (prélèvement forfaitaire unique) unless reduced under an applicable double-taxation treaty; this is a tax-stage parameter, not an FX convertibility barrier. Banks apply standard AML source-of-funds and UBO verification before executing any transfer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio apply in France or the eurozone. The SAS may freely retain export receipts in EUR or any convertible foreign currency. However, every transaction with a non-resident exceeding EUR 15,000 per calendar month must be reported to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistical purposes; this reporting applies to both inbound capital injections and outbound commercial settlements and is mandatory for resident legal entities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (via LCL)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for operating treasury flows. French-licensed EMIs (e.g., Qonto) and EEA EMIs passported into France under PSD2 (e.g., Revolut, Wise) offer multi-currency IBANs and FX accounts within 2-5 business days, with strong API connectivity for courier billing and disbursement automation. Legal constraint: passported EMIs cannot act as escrow agents or issue capital-blocked attestations. Offshore EMIs located outside the EEA (e.g., post-Brexit UK-only entities) cannot passport into France and require a full ACPR e-money licence or French payment-agent registration; their viability for core treasury purposes is Low and they should be used only as secondary convenience rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted under Articles L561-5 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code and the eIDAS Regulation, using video identification, qualified electronic signatures and digital UBO attestations. Physical attendance is not a statutory mandate. In practice, tier-1 banks require a remote videoconference with the legal representative and at least one additional signatory when the shareholding structure involves non-resident persons; certain banks reserve the right to request notarised or apostilled identity documents for directors residing in high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate ownership structure featuring UBOs resident in FATF grey-listed or non-cooperative tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS extrait K-bis; beneficial owner registry (RBE) extract; simplified group structure chart evidencing French economic substance; tax residency certificates for each UBO; payroll and office-lease documentation; sworn declaration of origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection credited from a third-party account or from a non-resident shareholder account inconsistent with declared shareholder identity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised or witnessed capital subscription agreement; shareholders' subscription list; originator bank statements covering 12 months; source-of-wealth evidence (salary slips, sale deeds, corporate financial statements); board resolution approving the inbound remittance with stated purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Express courier business classified as enhanced-risk trade sector with potential sanctions exposure on cross-border transport lanes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts with shippers and consignees; Incoterms matrix and airway-bill dataset; EU and OFAC sanctions-screening policy; denied-party screening reports; trade compliance manual; ISO 28000 supply-chain security certification if held.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material mismatch between projected turnover, declared ISIC 5320 activity, and expected bank flow volumes during onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma invoicing set and order-book pipeline; detailed operating model for cross-border express courier operations; 12-month cash-flow forecast; stamped customs declarations (DAU/ICS); committed client letters; route-planning and tracking-system audit trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident investor's bank to the SAS EUR IBAN held at a French bank. Field 70/72 must state 'Capital contribution / share subscription' and reference the shareholders' resolution and the constitutional act (acte de constitution). Use ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPG' or 'DINC' per the receiving bank's mapping. The receiving institution applies standard UBO and source-of-funds due diligence and records the operation as a direct investment for Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting (threshold EUR 15,000 per calendar month). Verification bundle: investor board resolution, subscription agreement, shareholder identity documents, and evidence that the originator holds the beneficial interest in the remitted funds; aggregation of unrelated third-party contributions triggers additional FATF Recommendation 16 tracing obligations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 for international agent settlements and low-ticket supplier disbursements; SWIFT MT202/202COV for interbank liquidity covering correspondent routing beyond the eurozone. SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for eurozone intraday payments; TARGET2 (T2) provides final euro settlement. For high-value consolidation-partner arrangements, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 with full transport document sets are used; cash-against-documents via MT103 remains acceptable for routine courier trade settlements.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate (impôt sur les sociétés).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject generally to annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% direct or indirect ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. Qualifying research and development expenditure may benefit from the research tax credit, generally at 30% of eligible expenditure in metropolitan France up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold, subject to statutory conditions. Certain innovation, investment, regional, or sectoral regimes may provide additional relief. Dividends received by a French parent from qualifying subsidiaries are generally subject to a 1% or 5% add-back, producing an effective participation-exemption taxation of approximately 0.25% or 1.25%, respectively, subject to conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Tax losses may generally be carried back only against the preceding fiscal year's profit, subject to an election and a EUR 1 million cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration's impots.gouv.fr professional portal using EDI-TDFC or an approved electronic filing provider. The return is accompanied by tax balance-sheet and profit-and-loss schedules, principally Forms 2050-SD through 2059-SD.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly corporate income tax instalment payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within three months after the end of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second business day after 1 May of the following year. The balance of corporate income tax is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, and by 15 May for a 31 December year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN number, fiscal year dates, legal form, tax office, and filing capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French SAS's own legal and tax identification details. Do not substitute the foreign shareholder's registration number. Identify a French permanent establishment separately if the filing concerns a non-French enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss determined from the French statutory accounts after tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French taxable results attributable to the French company or French permanent establishment. Exclude foreign branch income where an applicable treaty or exemption removes it from the French tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting result to taxable result, including permanent non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and other book-to-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reverse non-deductible head-office charges, unsupported management fees, non-arm's-length related-party expenses, and expenses not incurred in the French business. Apply treaty allocation principles to permanent-establishment expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of current-year losses, carried-forward losses, or carried-back losses against taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% limitation to carried-forward losses. Maintain evidence of the origin, amount, and prior utilization of each loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2050-SD to 2057-SD, balance sheet and profit-and-loss schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, payables, inventory, turnover, operating expenses, financial income, and exceptional items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use French accounting records and reconcile intercompany balances with the foreign parent and affiliates. Separately identify cross-border royalties, interest, service fees, commissions, and recharge arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholding structure, subsidiaries, participations, and relevant intra-group information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the foreign parent, ultimate beneficial ownership where required, controlled subsidiaries, and participation-exemption positions. Retain ownership-period and tax-subject-to-tax evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and payment of the final corporate income tax balance after instalments, tax credits, and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance with instalment payments, research tax credits, foreign tax credits, and any withholding taxes. Payment must be made electronically by the French entity or its authorized tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly corporate income tax instalment declaration and payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay instalments electronically based on prior-year or estimated current-year liability. New companies may have no instalment obligation for their first accounting period, subject to statutory rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Eligible research and development expenditure and calculation of the research tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenditure incurred by the French taxpayer or qualifying French research arrangements. Maintain technical files, personnel records, subcontractor approvals, and project-level cost evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of controlled transactions, transfer pricing methods, counterparties, jurisdictions, and documentation status where the statutory threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with foreign related parties, including management services, logistics support, financing, intellectual property, insurance, and cost allocations. Align all amounts with the Local File and general ledger.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge on tax due, potentially increased to 40% or 80% for deliberate failure or fraudulent conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, calculated from the statutory due date; France does not generally impose a universal daily surcharge for corporate income tax filing. Incorrect filings may also trigger a 40% deliberate-evasion penalty or an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres, abusive-law conduct, or concealed activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1447-C-SD initial CFE declaration and Form 1447-M-SD annual modification declaration, filed through the French business tax area on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual or event-driven, depending on establishment, acquisition, relocation, and modification circumstances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The initial CFE declaration is generally due by 31 December of the year in which the establishment is created. Modification information is generally due by the first business day following 1 May of the relevant year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, establishment SIRET, address, commencement date, activity code, and business premises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident courier group operating through a French SAS must report the French establishment and not merely the foreign headquarters.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Premises, taxable rental value, employee information, and business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include French sorting, warehousing, dispatch, office, and operational premises. Reconcile premises data with lease contracts and payroll records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or inaccurate CFE declarations may cause assessment based on available information, loss of relief, tax reassessment, and general tax-procedure penalties. Unpaid CFE is subject to late-payment interest and collection surcharges under the French Tax Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax on dividends and similar distributions paid to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may eliminate withholding where the parent, ownership, minimum holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's competent tax authority and complete the applicable French forms, generally Form 5000 for residence certification together with Form 5001 for dividends, Form 5002 for interest, or Form 5003 for royalties. Submit the forms to the French payer or withholding agent before applying the reduced rate or exemption. Confirm beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test requirements where applicable, ownership percentage, holding period, and anti-conduit status. If relief at source is unavailable, withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund through the French tax administration using the applicable treaty claim procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and possible EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including certain payments to non-cooperative or non-cooperating jurisdictions, anti-abuse situations, and specific statutory categories. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and from 0% to 10% or 15% for royalties, but the applicable bilateral treaty must be checked. French domestic anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, deductibility, and interest-limitation rules remain applicable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File documentation is generally mandatory where the French entity or group satisfies the EUR 400 million threshold based on turnover or gross assets, or where the entity is controlled by or controls an entity meeting the statutory threshold. A Country-by-Country Report generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million. The annual transfer pricing summary declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at a EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, or in specified cases involving significant controlled transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless required under French transfer pricing, beneficial-ownership, treaty anti-abuse, general anti-abuse, controlled foreign company, interest limitation, withholding-tax, and permanent-establishment rules. The French SAS should maintain real French decision-making, operational personnel, premises, assets, risk control, books, bank activity, and commercial functions consistent with its courier business. A conduit company, artificial invoicing entity, or entity lacking control over risks may lose treaty benefits, deductions, or tax residency recognition.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing French turnover, fabricating expenses, maintaining parallel books, deliberately understating taxable profit, or submitting materially false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may reach 80% of tax avoided, in addition to assessed tax and late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of EUR 500,000, with aggravated penalties of up to seven years and EUR 3 million in serious cases, including use of shell entities, foreign accounts, or organized fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, imprisonment, management bans, and civil claims. Courts may impose director liability for tax debts where fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated management failures made collection impossible. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require a competent judicial or administrative measure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting French courier profits to a foreign affiliate through excessive royalties, management fees, financing costs, commissions, procurement charges, or underpriced services without arm's-length evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions, recharacterization of distributions, withholding-tax assessment, late-payment interest, and penalties generally ranging from 40% for deliberate conduct to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres. Missing or inadequate documentation may support a transfer pricing adjustment and a specific documentation-related penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and, where intentional evasion is established, criminal liability. They should approve documented policies, maintain contemporaneous comparables, and ensure that contractual terms reflect actual functions, assets, and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating a French operating depot, sorting facility, sales operation, dependent agent, or logistics function as having no French taxable presence despite regular local business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate income tax, VAT, payroll and local tax assessments may be imposed on attributable profits, with interest and penalties. Treaty relief may be denied where the factual permanent-establishment conditions are satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may face civil liability for intentional misrepresentation and criminal exposure where the structure was designed to conceal a taxable presence. Personal exposure is fact-dependent and is not created solely by a tax assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying cross-border shipments, falsifying customs values or origin, improperly applying export or intra-EU VAT exemptions, or failing to account for import VAT and customs duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of VAT and customs duties, interest, administrative fines, seizure of goods, suspension or loss of customs simplifications, and potentially criminal prosecution for smuggling or fraudulent declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may be personally prosecuted for intentional false declarations or organized fraud. Civil recovery and professional authorization consequences may apply; imprisonment depends on the specific customs or tax offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS solely as a pass-through vehicle, issuing invoices without personnel or capacity, routing payments through an unsupported foreign principal, or claiming treaty benefits without beneficial ownership or commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, application of withholding tax, reassessment of corporate income tax, disallowance of expenses, penalties for abuse of law or fraudulent manoeuvres, and possible application of anti-conduit and controlled foreign company principles.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for fraudulent management, tax fraud, abuse of corporate assets, or insolvency-related misconduct. Veil piercing is exceptional and requires serious personal misconduct; it is not automatic merely because the company is wholly foreign-owned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting suspicious cash or third-party payments, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions screening, structuring transactions, or failing to report suspicious activity to TRACFIN where legally required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory sanctions may include warnings, reprimands, fines, business restrictions, withdrawal of authorization, and criminal sanctions for money laundering or terrorist financing. Criminal money laundering may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated penalties of up to 10 years and EUR 750,000 in specified cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and responsible employees may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, facilitation, or deliberate failure to implement required controls. Asset freezing, confiscation, and judicial travel restrictions may apply where ordered by competent authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transporting prohibited goods, servicing sanctioned persons, routing shipments through embargoed jurisdictions, or processing payments involving blocked parties without authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative freezing, seizure, license restrictions, customs measures, substantial criminal fines, and imprisonment may apply under French, European Union, and applicable international sanctions regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be prosecuted for intentional or negligent sanctions violations, depending on the applicable measure. Corporate authorization and banking relationships may be suspended or terminated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees to non-residents without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate, or failing to remit withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French company may owe the unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties, commonly 10% for late payment and up to 40% or 80% for deliberate or fraudulent conduct. Treaty-relief claims may be rejected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for deliberate non-remittance, fraudulent concealment, or serious management misconduct. Personal liability is not automatic for an ordinary administrative error corrected promptly.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to incur debt while insolvent, preferring related parties, diverting corporate assets, failing to file for insolvency within the statutory period, or paying shareholder distributions that impair creditor protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French insolvency courts may impose asset shortfall liability, prohibition from managing companies, bankruptcy-related sanctions, annulment of suspect-period transactions, and criminal penalties for bankruptcy offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be ordered to contribute to all or part of the company's insufficiency of assets and may face management bans or imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy. A general travel ban is not automatic and requires a judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain statutory accounts, filing materially inaccurate annual accounts, omitting beneficial-owner information, or failing to preserve tax, payroll, customs, and transfer pricing records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Formal notices, fines, tax reassessment, refusal of deductions, judicial orders to file, and criminal sanctions for false accounts or obstruction may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and directors may incur civil liability for losses caused by deficient governance and criminal liability for intentional false statements, obstruction, or misuse of corporate assets.
